newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns Irish Permanent ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns Irish Permanent ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it had assigned a long-term rating of A and a short-term A1 to Irish Permanent Plc, the third largest Irish bank.

Irish Permanent converted from a building society in 1994 and its core business remains residential mortgage lending, although it has diversified into other areas of finance in recent years, IBCA said.
"Its record of consistently good performance has been helped by a stable housing market in Ireland," the agency said.
"Profitability is high, capital ratios are strong, and credit losses have been negligible, to a large extent reflecting Irish Permanent's conservative lending criteria," an IBCA statement said.

"In view of the strength of the Irish economy and the favourable outlook for the housing market, IBCA considers that Irish Permanent should be able to continue to deliver a strong performance," it said.
